title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from 'comme plus haut'). A is the ring of integers of a finite extension K of Q_p, with residue degree f, ramification index e, and h = ef. q = p^f, and k is a perfect field over F_q. For the statements as written (F^f being an element of A) one needs effectively k = F_q, with W = W(k). G_0 is a Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) group of height h over k with an action of A. Its Dieudonné module M is free of rank h over W, hence free of rank 1 over A⊗_{Z_p}W. Since W contains W(F_q), there is a decomposition A⊗_{Z_p}W ≅ ∏_{ν=0}^{f-1} A⊗_{W(F_q),σ^ν}W, which is A^{[0,f-1]} when k = F_q. The semilinear F permutes the f factors cyclically, sending factor ν to factor ν+1. So F^f is A-linear on a rank-one A⊗W-module, and over F_q it is multiplication by some ϖ ∈ A. On factor ν, F is π^{r_ν}·(unit), so dim G_0 = length(M/FM) = Σ r_ν = v(ϖ) = lg_A(A/ϖA).

Proposition. The following are equivalent:
(i) dim G_0 = 1;
(ii) F^f = π_{G_0} for a uniformizer π of A;
(iii) M ≅ Ω⊗_{Z_p}W = Ω⊗_A(A⊗W), with Ω an invertible A-module, and F = id⊗σ + pr_ν[(π−1)⊗σ]. That is, F = σ on every factor except factor ν, where it is π·σ.
The index ν records through which of the f embeddings F_q → k the group A acts on the one-dimensional Lie algebra. The case of the given embedding is the 'strict' formal A-module, i.e. the reduction of a Lubin–Tate group, whose q-Frobenius is [π]. The margin note says the f groups obtained for different ν are pairwise non-isomorphic as groups with A-action, but all isogenous.

Second NB (A-height 1, arbitrary dimension). M is given by data (Ω, r_ν, u) with 0 ≤ r_ν ≤ e and u ∈ A^*, where F on factor ν is π^{r_ν} times a unit. This is the p-divisible analogue of Raynaud's exponents for F-vector space schemes.
- A-equivariant homomorphisms G_0 → G'_0 correspond to F-compatible A⊗W-linear maps v = (v_ν): M' → M.
- The relation v_{ν+1}F' = F v_ν gives v_{ν+1} = π^{Σ_0^ν(r_i − r'_i)}·(unit)·σ(v_ν).
- Closing the cycle at ν = f forces ϖ = ϖ', i.e. F^f_{G_0} = F^f_{G'_0}. This is a Tate-type criterion: Frobenius determines the isogeny class.
- The Hom module is then H ⊂ Hom(Ω',Ω), consisting of those v_0 with v(v_0) + Σ_0^ν r_i − Σ_0^ν r'_i ≥ 0 for 0 ≤ ν ≤ f−2.
The purpose is to describe BT groups with formal multiplication by A over finite fields, presumably with a view to lifting (Lubin–Tate theory) in the crystalline / Dieudonné context of the 'Cristaux' notes.
errors: Statement (ii) and 'F^f = ϖ ∈ A' are only literally correct over k = F_q (or after choosing an F_q-structure). Over a larger perfect k, F^f is σ^f-semilinear, and the decomposition of A⊗W is A⊗_{W(F_q)}W, not A^{[0,f-1]}. Grothendieck's 'comme plus haut' presumably fixes this.
In the Hom computation, the integrality condition should also include the case ν = −1 (v_0 itself integral). That case is implicit in v_0 ∈ Hom(Ω',Ω).
Minor: Ω invertible over the DVR A is free, so Ω is just a canonical bookkeeping device. Fine, no error.

ideas.what: Classification of A-height-one p-divisible groups with A-action over F_q via Dieudonné modules decomposed along embeddings, with exponents r_ν
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné modules of π-divisible / O-divisible groups of O-height 1; p-divisible analogue of Raynaud's F-vector space schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud (1974) for finite group schemes; Hazewinkel, Drinfeld (1976) for formal A-modules; later Hilbert modular literature (Goren, Andreatta–Goren)
ideas.where_published: Not in the published Barsotti–Tate notes (Montréal 1970) as far as known

ideas.what: dim G_0 = 1 iff F^f = [π] for a uniformizer; f non-isomorphic but isogenous forms indexed by the Lie-algebra embedding ν
ideas.modern_name: Reductions of Lubin–Tate groups; strict vs non-strict formal A-modules

ideas.what: Nonzero A-homomorphism exists iff F^f coincide; Hom given as an explicit sub-A-module via valuation conditions on partial sums of r_ν − r'_ν
ideas.modern_name: Tate's isogeny theorem for p-divisible groups over finite fields, in the O-module setting

missed.claim: An early (c. 1967–71) explicit p-divisible version of what became Raynaud's 1974 parametrization of F_q-vector space schemes by exponents r_ν ∈ [0,e], including the Hom computation via partial sums. This is mathematically standard today, so it is only of historical-priority interest.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck working out Raynaud/Breuil–Kisin-style embedding-wise exponent bookkeeping in his crystal notes. It is of historical interest only; no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, clean, but standard Dieudonné-module classification of Lubin–Tate-type BT groups with A-action over F_q. The content is now textbook / Raynaud-style. Its slight historical interest lies in its early date and the explicit exponent bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: The first line reads like 'Dans le cas où ...' (an unfinished heading), not mathematical content.
In (iii), the triple is (Ω, ν, π): 'Ω un module inversible sur A, 0 ≤ ν ≤ f−1, π une uniformisante de A'.
'conditions équivalentes' follows 'Alors'; the struck-out words are an earlier 'conditions équivalentes'.
Margin NB: 'Tous ces groupes (pour ν permis) sont distincts deux à deux, i.e. non isomorphes avec action de A, ... mais isogènes ...', with mention of F_q = F_{p^f}.
The second NB concerns the general case of A-height 1 (dim arbitrary, data Ω', r'_ν, u' ∈ A^*). It is not restricted to dim G_0 = 1.
